title: Generation of Cationic Nanoliposomes for the Efficient Delivery of In Vitro Transcribed Messenger RNA
protocol: Dissolve DC-cholesterol and DOPE lipids in chloroform to achieve a final concentration of 25 mg/mL.
Store the dissolved lipids at -20°C.
Mix 40 µL of dissolved DC-cholesterol with 80 µL of dissolved DOPE in a glass flask.
Place the lipids on ice during pipetting.
Vaporize chloroform for 15 min under an argon gas flow.
Fill a desiccator with silica gel, place the open glass flask inside, and apply a vacuum overnight to evaporate remaining chloroform.
Rehydrate the formed lipid film with 1 mL of nuclease-free water.
Vortex the suspension for 15 min.
Place the suspension into a sonication bath for 1 h.
Press the lipid suspension through the membrane from one syringe to the other, 20x – 25x, using an extruder.
Prepare the eGFP-encoding mRNA following the published protocol.
Amplify the eGFP sequence from the plasmid using 0.7 µM forward and reverse primers and the polymerase kit with PCR.
Mix 20 μL of commercial buffer, 20 μL of 5x mix from the polymerase kit, 7 μL of each primer, 25 ng of eGFP plasmid, and 2 μL of polymerase in a total volume of 100 µL with nuclease-free H2O.
Run the PCR cycles following the protocol in Table 1.
Purify the eGFP-encoding DNA sequence using the PCR purification kit.
Mix the PCR solution with 500 μL of binding buffer from the kit and use it to fill purification columns.
Centrifuge the columns at maximum speed for 1 min and discard the filtrate.
Add 750 μL of wash buffer I to the column.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 1 min and discard the filtrate.
Repeat centrifugation step once more.
Transfer the column to a fresh 1.5-mL tube.
Add 20 μL of nuclease-free H2O to the column.
Incubate for 1 min.
Centrifuge for 1 min at maximum speed.
Repeat incubation and centrifugation steps.
Measure DNA concentration with a photometer.
Store DNA at -20 °C.
Perform gel electrophoresis for DNA quality analysis.
Add 0.5 g of agarose in TBE buffer and heat until completely dissolved.
Add 5 μL of gel-staining solution to the liquid agarose.
Fill the solution into the gel chamber and wait for polymerization.
Mix 200 ng of DNA with 2 μL of 6x loading dye.
Fill up mixture to an end volume of 12 μL.
Pipette a DNA ladder and the DNA sample into the gel wells.
Run electrophoresis for 1 h at 100 V.
Analyze the gel using a gel-analyzing station under UV light.
For in vitro transcription, mix ingredients as per Table 2 instructions.
Replace 1.5 μL of methyl-CTP with Cy3-CTP diluted in nuclease-free H2O during eGFP mRNA transcription to achieve Cy3-labeling.
Incubate the IVT reaction mix for 4 h at 37 °C.
Add 1 μL of DNase I from the T7 polymerase kit and incubate it for 15 min at 37 °C to digest the DNA template.
Fill up the IVT mix to a volume of 100 µL with nuclease-free H2O.
Add 350 µL of lysis buffer and mix by pipetting up and down.
Add 250 µL of 100% ethanol and mix again.
Pipette the mix into the cleanup columns.
Centrifuge for 15 s at 8,000 x g and discard the filtrate.
Add 500 µL of washing buffer to a column and centrifuge for 15 s at 8,000 x g.
Remove the filtrate.
Wash the column once with 500 µL of wash buffer and centrifuge for 2 min at 8,000 x g.
Move the column into a fresh 1.5-mL reaction tube.
Elute the mRNA by adding 20 µL of nuclease-free H2O to the column membrane and incubate for 1 min.
Centrifuge the eluted mixture for 1 min at maximum speed.
Remove the phosphate groups from the mRNA using a dephosphorylation kit.
Add 4.5 μL of 10x phosphatase buffer and 1 µL of phosphatase to the mRNA.
Incubate for 1 h at 37 °C.
Purify the mRNA again, following steps 2.5.1 - 2.5.7.
Measure the mRNA concentration with a photometer.
Prepare an agarose gel as described in steps 2.3.9 - 2.3.10.
Mix 3.3 µL of formamide, 1 µL of 37% formaldehyde, 1 µL of 10x MEN, and 1.7 µL of 6x loading dye with 200 ng of mRNA.
Fill the mixture up to 10 µL with nuclease-free H2O for each sample and RNA marker.
Incubate the mix for 10 min at 65 °C for mRNA denaturation.
Load the wells of the gel with the mRNA and RNA marker.
Run the gel for 1 h at 100 V.
Analyze the gel using a gel doc station with UV light.
Thaw the synthetic mRNA on ice.
Vortex the thawed synthetic mRNA.
Centrifuge the vorticed mRNA briefly before opening the tube.
Mix 10 µL of synthetic mRNA (mRNA concentration is 100 ng/µL) with NLp suspension at specified volumes (1 µL, 2.5 µL, 5 µL, 10 µL, or 20 µL).
Centrifuge the mixture briefly.
Incubate for 20 min at room temperature (RT) for nanolipoplex formation.
Add 1 mL of regular cell medium to the nanolipoplexes.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Thaw the fluorescent dye on ice.
Dilute the fluorescent dye 1:200 for a high-range assay and 1:2,000 for a low-range assay.
Prepare the working solution directly before use.
Use 1 mL of a 2 µg/mL stock solution of eGFP mRNA in nuclease-free H2O to prepare high-range and low-range standard curves.
Dilute the 2 µg/mL eGFP mRNA stock solution 1:20 to achieve a final concentration of 100 ng/mL for the low-range standard.
Keep the mRNA on ice to avoid degradation.
Combine 1 µg of eGFP mRNA (10 µL) and 7.5 µg of NLps (2.5 µL).
Incubate the mixture for 20 min at room temperature.
Add 1 mL of nuclease-free H2O to form nanolipoplexes.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Add 1 mL of 1:200 or 1:2,000 RNA fluorescent dye working solution to the encapsulated samples and standards.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature in the dark.
Pipette the standards and samples in duplicates into a black 96-well plate.
Measure the fluorescence at 530 nm on a microplate reader.
Plate 1.5 x 10^5 A549 cells/well of a 12-well plate 1 day prior to transfection.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in regular cell medium (DMEM/high glucose with 10% fetal bovine serum [FBS], 2 mM L-glutamine, 1% penicillin/streptomycin) for 24 h before transfection.
Wash the prepared cells once with 1 mL/well PBS (without Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺).
Add 1 mL of prepared nanolipoplex mixture containing 1 µg of eGFP mRNA encapsulated into NLps ranging from 1-µL to 20-µL volumes, to one well of the prepared plate with A549 cells.
Incubate the nanolipoplex suspension with the cells for 24 hours to analyze transfection efficacy.
Incubate the nanolipoplex suspension with the cells for 24 hours and then again for an additional 72 hours to analyze cell viability after transfection.
Remove the supernatant from the cells and wash them with 1 mL/well of PBS without Ca2+/Mg2+ ions.
Trypsinize the cells using 500 µL/well of trypsin/EDTA at 37 °C for 3 minutes.
Inactivate the trypsin by adding an equal volume (500 µL/well) of regular FBS-containing medium.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 400 x g and carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of PBS without Ca2+/Mg2+ ions.
Resuspend the cells in 300 µL of 1x fixation solution and transfer them into flow cytometry tubes.
Analyze the resuspended cells at 488 nm using a flow cytometer.
Vortex the cell suspension directly before measuring for flow cytometry analysis.
Fix the cells with 1 mL/well of methanol stored at -20 °C.
Add 500 µL/well of DAPI solution (300 nM in PBS) and incubate for 5 minutes in the dark.
Remove the DAPI solution and wash the cells again with 1 mL/well of methanol stored at -20 °C.
Analyze the fixed and stained cells using a fluorescence microscope.
Dissolve 5 mg of MTT in 1 mL of RPMI without phenol red.
Further dilute the MTT solution 1:10 in RPMI to a final concentration of 0.5 mg/mL.
Wash transfected cells three times with 1 mL/well PBS without Ca2+/Mg2+.
Remove all remaining regular cell medium completely.
Add 500 µL/well of the 1:10 diluted MTT solution to the cells and incubate for 4 hours at 37 °C.
Remove the MTT solution from the cells after incubation.
Add 500 µL/well DMSO to the cells and incubate for 10 minutes at 37 °C.
Pipette the DMSO solution in triplets into a clear-bottom 96-well plate.
Measure absorbance at 540 nm using a microplate reader.
